feedback: Decision: approve. The candidate is the best raced design (iteration 6, score 372.74: x = ±0.032 m, kp 3.0, kd 0.40, ki 0.30, base_speed 1.5, footprint 0.016 m, last_direction) with one change, the two outer sensors moved from x = ±0.032 m to ±0.040 m. The inner sensors stay at 0 and ±0.016 m, the weights stay antisymmetric at (-1.6, -0.8, 0, 0.8, 1.6), and every other field is held, so the step is single-variable. The evidence is the spread trend in earlier races: widening from ±0.016 to ±0.024 m raised the score from 103.99 region to 124.80 (iteration 1 to 3 for the spread alone, with oval finishes rising), and widening from ±0.024 to ±0.032 m raised oval finishes from 3 to 7 and cut s-bend line losses from 2.0 to 1.05 (iteration 3 to 5). Iteration 9 showed kp 3.25 lowered the score to 306.17, so kp returns to 3.0. Iteration 8 showed kd 0.50 lowered the score to 352.73, so kd stays at 0.40. Iteration 7 showed base_speed 1.3 cut oval finishes to 7, so speed stays at 1.5. The candidate is valid: all positions are inside the ±0.08 m limit, the footprint is in the allowed set, and line_loss is last_direction. The main risk is that the outermost sensor sits 0.040 m from centre, close to the 0.06 m off-track limit, and that the weights give a weaker centre response, which could raise oscillation on the oval (already 0.285 at iteration 6). I make no claim about how it will perform. With one iteration after this one, racing now gives the telemetry needed for the final choice. Read the race as follows. If oval finishes stay at 17 or more and the score holds at or above 372.74, keep ±0.040 m as the new best. If oval finishes fall below 17 or the score falls below 372.74, revert to ±0.032 m with kp 3.0 and kd 0.40, which is the safe fallback for the final evaluation. In either case, check whether s-bend and slalom line losses fell (the s-bend had 1.05 at ±0.032 m) and where max_error peaks.
requested_changes: If the score holds at or above 372.74 with oval finishes of 17 or more, keep x = ±0.040 m for the outer sensors and test nothing else in that step, since widening has produced the largest consistent gains (iterations 0 to 5).

If oval finishes fall below 17 or the score falls below 372.74, revert the outer sensors to x = ±0.032 m with kp 3.0, kd 0.40, ki 0.30 and base_speed 1.5 (iteration 6, score 372.74), since kp 3.25 (iteration 9) and kd 0.50 (iteration 8) both lowered the score.

If steering_oscillation on the oval rises well above 0.29 (iteration 6 value) at ±0.040 m, try kd 0.45 with the same spread, because the extra damping at kd 0.30 to 0.40 is what raised oval finishes from 7 to 19 (iterations 5 to 6).
